inline_comments.comment: `@react-aria/live-announcer` is imported here inside the `code/addons/vitest` workspace, but the package is only declared as a dependency in `code/core/package.json`. Per monorepo conventions, each workspace must declare its own dependencies in its own `package.json` — you cannot rely on a sibling workspace's `node_modules` being visible at runtime in all environments. Add `"@react-aria/live-announcer": "^3.4.4"` to the `devDependencies` of `code/addons/vitest/package.json`.

Import order violation. `@react-aria/live-announcer` is a third-party package and should appear *after* the Storybook package imports (`storybook/manager-api`, `storybook/test`, `storybook/theming`). Per project conventions the order is: (1) built-in/platform, (2) Storybook packages, (3) other third-party, (4) relative imports.

This is a deep cross-package relative import from the `addons/vitest` workspace into `core/src/manager/utils/`. The project rule is to import across package boundaries via public package exports, not via relative paths into another package's source directory — such paths are fragile under restructuring and bypass the package's intended API surface.

Either: (a) export `toHaveLiveRegion` from a public entry point of `code/core` (e.g., `storybook/internal/manager-utils`), or (b) move/copy the utility into the `addons/vitest` package itself since it is only used there.

The assertion `await expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion(...)` is not wrapped in `waitFor`. The `@react-aria/live-announcer` implementation may batch or debounce DOM updates, meaning the live-region element may not be present synchronously after `mount` resolves. Without `waitFor`, the assertion fires exactly once and cannot retry — making all three announcement stories potentially flaky. Wrap with `await waitFor(() => expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion(...))`. The same applies to the assertions in `AnnouncesTestRunFinished` (line 365) and `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed` (line 391).

general_comments.comment: The PR description states that `extend-to-be-announced` was added as a devDependency in `code/core/package.json` and registered in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts` via `import 'extend-to-be-announced/vitest'`, and advertises `toBeAnnounced` as the assertion API. None of these changes appear in the diff. The implementation instead uses the custom `toHaveLiveRegion` DOM-inspection matcher. The description should be updated to match the actual implementation, or the intended `extend-to-be-announced` integration should be completed. As written, the description misleads reviewers about which assertion mechanism is active.

`code/core/src/manager/utils/toHaveLiveRegion.ts` is a Vitest custom matcher — a purely test-support utility — placed in a production source directory (`src/manager/utils/`). Production utility directories are typically included in bundle analysis and can be imported by non-test code. Consider placing test-only utilities in a dedicated location (e.g., `src/manager/__testUtils__/`) and ensure it is excluded from any production bundle entry points, to make the test-only nature of the file clear and prevent accidental inclusion.
